guidance.procedure: Identify the precise dimension tested: information content, communication medium, identification requirement, confidentiality of negotiations or the agreement, independent development, or third-party acquisition. Read each definition or exception through syntactic and numbered-list closure. Include a governing definition or exception lead-in when it supplies the legal relation, plus every independently responsive item. Compare quantifiers exactly: “only,” “all,” and “any” matter. Broad media language does not itself establish non-technical content, and commercial background does not necessarily resolve an exclusive technical definition. For identification, distinguish mandatory marking from contextual or reasonable-person standards. For oral information, distinguish inclusion from a later confirmation procedure. For exceptions, distinguish independent development, prior possession, public availability, and third-party receipt. After deciding the relation, remove headings, list markers, background, and neighboring provisions that do not directly establish the target proposition.

Normalize each provision into actor, required or permitted act, object, trigger, duration, and any exception. Keep request, termination, expiration, abandonment of discussions, and other triggering events distinct. A duty to return or destroy upon request does not establish a termination-triggered duty. Likewise, an agreement’s term does not by itself establish that confidentiality obligations survive termination. For post-return possession, compare polarity directly: an express backup, archival, dispute, or similar retention exception can support permission, while an obligation to return or destroy all material or retain no copies can oppose it. Search the entire source for independently responsive survival language, including duration, termination-effect, return, and enforcement provisions. Include each operative provision that independently settles continued effect, but exclude a nearby term or return sentence that supplies no responsive survival rule.

Parse the operative actor, action, object, recipient class, modality, conditions, and exceptions before comparing the hypothesis. Treat disclosure, copying, use, solicitation, hiring, reverse engineering, and confidentiality as separate actions even when adjacent. For sharing, expand incorporated recipient definitions: employees alone are not equivalent to employees, agents, contractors, consultants, or professional advisers. A structure such as “shall not disclose unless necessary and bound” is a conditional permission, not an absolute prohibition; preserve its conditions. Include both the operative permission or prohibition and a recipient definition when both are needed to express the covered class. For copying, require copy, reproduce, or equivalent conduct and its condition; a general confidentiality or ownership clause is insufficient. For limited use, scan for every independently responsive purpose restriction rather than stopping at the first. For solicitation provisions split across spans, read through the complete subject, prohibition, parallel acts, and exceptions.

Use separate branches for the two targets. For compelled-disclosure notice, locate every disclosure mechanism—general legal process and any special statutory or regulatory route—and require language imposing notice, notification, an opportunity to object, or an equivalent communication duty. Collect independently responsive notice provisions across mechanisms, but do not automatically include a section lead-in, the mere permission to disclose, or a limitation to the compelled portion. For no-license propositions, inspect the full no-rights or no-license passage and collect each independent denial of a patent, intellectual-property, title, use, or confidentiality-related right that directly answers the proposition. When the operative sentence is divided across spans, retain it through grammatical completion. Do not infer a license denial merely from ownership, confidentiality, or restricted-use language.

Apply an exact predicate gate before deciding relation. For scope, identify stated content categories and any exclusivity term; generic “information,” communication media, access, or default confidentiality does not establish technical-only or non-technical breadth. For identification, require an operative mark, identify, designate, or awareness condition; keep oral inclusion separate from later confirmation. For agreement confidentiality, require language covering the agreement, its subject matter, terms, or negotiations. Name each exception category—independent development, prior possession, public availability, or third-party receipt—and never substitute one for another. Then make a separate whole-source membership pass: follow grammatical and numbered-list closure, include independently responsive definitions or exceptions, and exclude headings or neighboring procedures that do not establish the tested predicate.

operations.rationale: The current batch repeatedly converted broad confidentiality or media language into unsupported scope, identification, and oral-inclusion conclusions, and interchanged public-domain, third-party, and independent-development exceptions. The prior publication also coincided with definition-related label regressions and frequent incomplete or extra memberships. This update replaces abstract reminders with observable predicate gates and uses shorter contrasting evidence while removing a costly false-citation example that did not prevent those errors.

guidance.procedure: For every lifecycle clause, record actor, act, object, trigger, coverage, duration, and exception. Decide return from the trigger stated in that same operative rule: termination or a source-defined event ending the transaction or relationship may qualify, but a request-triggered duty cannot borrow termination language from a separate survival clause. Decide survival only from an express duration or termination-effect rule, not from confidentiality, remedies, severability, or the agreement’s term alone. Decide retention by coverage and polarity: an express archival, backup, dispute, or legal-retention exception can permit possession; an all-information, all-copies, retain-no-copies, or backup-deletion command can oppose it, while a limited tangible-document return duty may leave it unsettled. Assign each span by function and collect every independently responsive rule without attaching neighboring mechanics.

operations.rationale: Observed answers repeatedly merged request with termination, treated agreement duration or remedies as survival, and assigned return mechanics to retention evidence. They also truncated multi-condition retention exceptions. The revision makes the same-clause trigger and object coverage executable, preserves both retention polarities, and removes the earlier term-sentence contrast after the prior publication produced lifecycle label harms despite already mentioning the distinction.

guidance.procedure: First locate the exact operative verb: reverse engineer, solicit or contact, disclose, copy or reproduce, or use. Do not substitute confidentiality, ownership, access, recipient status, or a section heading for that act. Normalize actor, modality, object, recipient class, conditions, and exceptions. Keep employees distinct from outside advisers, consultants, agents, contractors, affiliates, and other third parties; expand a defined recipient class only when the operative disclosure rule incorporates it. A prohibition with a need-to-know, consent, or binding-obligation exception is conditional permission for the covered class, not automatically an absolute prohibition. For copying, distinguish permission or prohibition to copy from a rule merely governing markings on copies. Follow split sentences and every conjunctive condition through completion. After relation choice, include all independent purpose restrictions or recipient rules, but exclude recitals, definitions of status, remedies, headings, and adjacent clauses that add no responsive act.

operations.rationale: Current errors conflated employee access with outside-third-party sharing, role definitions with permission, copying conditions with permission to copy, and confidentiality definitions with limited use. Fragmented solicitation and recipient conditions were also truncated. The update supplies explicit action and recipient gates with opposed sharing and copying boundaries, while pruning the former nonmember and longer examples because the actual paired runs showed substantial overcitation and no evidence-acquisition gain from the published bank.

guidance.procedure: Use two independent predicate gates. For compelled notice, first locate a legal, regulatory, judicial, subpoena, public-records, or comparable compelled-disclosure mechanism; then require an operative duty to notify, communicate with, or give the discloser an opportunity to object. A permission to disclose, a compelled-portion limit, or a section lead-in alone is not notice evidence. Scan separately for each mechanism and include every independently responsive notice rule, following any split sentence to completion. For no-license, require an express denial of a license, right, title, use right, proprietary interest, or intellectual-property right. Confidentiality, ownership, access, return, restricted use, or the absence of a grant cannot substitute for that denial. Include each independent denial and its grammatical completion, but exclude headings and adjacent provisions that merely describe ownership or permitted use.

operations.rationale: The batch preserved some notice decisions but still omitted mechanism lead-ins or added non-notice limitations, while unrelated definitions and restricted-use clauses were repeatedly labeled as license grants or denials. The stricter dual predicate gate directly addresses those source-observable failures. Retaining one multi-mechanism notice witness and one concise no-license witness, while dropping the prior false-citation contrast, reduces materialized cost and avoids treating a local nonmember excerpt as a general exclusion rule.

Upon termination of this Agreement, Receiving Party will, within two (2) weeks of written request from Disclosing Party, return all documents concerning the Proprietary Information and NREL Protected Information and all copies of any such documents to Disclosing Party, or certify in writing their destruction, with the exception of copies of Proprietary Information and NREL Protected Information made as a matter of routine information technology or legal backup, provided that such copies will continue to be subject to the confidentiality obligations set forth in this Agreement and may only be used in resolving a dispute between the Parties regarding this Agreement.
This duty to withhold Confidential Information survives any expiration or termination of this Agreement as provided herein.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, if required by law, the Designated Individual may retain documents containing Confidential Information, SSI, or PCII only if:
(1) the TJPA is notified in writing of such retention; and
(2) the Designated Individual continues to abide by the requirements of this Agreement with respect to protection of Confidential Information, SSI, or PCII.

Buyer will not circumvent Seller and/or Broker by contacting any person or persons involved with the Business including, without limitation, landlords, employees, suppliers or customers.
2. Subject to the provisions of Clauses 4 and 7 hereof, the Receiving Party undertakes:

(a) to keep confidential and not disclose to any third party, except with the written permission of the Disclosing Party, any part, or the whole, of any Proprietary Information disclosed to it under this Agreement;
(d) to restrict access to the Proprietary Information disclosed to it under the terms of this Agreement to those of its employees and officers who need to know the same for the Purpose.

Recipient shall not disclose Confidential Information to any of its Representatives or Representatives of its Affiliates, except as required to carry out the Purpose under this Agreement for the benefit of Deere and its Affiliates.
“Representative” shall mean any officer, director, employee, contractor, agent, supplier, or advisor of its respective entity.

“Affiliate” shall mean any corporation, partnership, or other entity that, either directly or indirectly, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where control is defined as having more than a fifty percent (50%) controlling interest.

 Volunteer, Trainer or Evaluator agrees not to, without prior written consent from Companion Paws and The LifeLine Canada Foundation, divulge any Confidential Information to third parties or copy documents containing any Confidential Information.
Recipient shall not use Confidential Information except as required to carry out the Purpose under this Agreement.
